# Proposal — the Weekly Digest agent

*(Fixture artifact: a plan submitted for review, written the way a real user writes
one. Read it cold. Its provenance and the bar it is scored against are in `run.md`,
which the runtime under test does not read. Do not edit this file.)*

## What I want

Every Sunday I want a one-page summary of my vault waiting for me: what I added
this week, what changed, what's overdue for review, and what's still sitting in the
Inbox. I want it mailed to me so I read it on my phone before the week starts.

## How it should work

A new **Digest agent** lives in `System/Agents/digest/`. It hangs off the weekly
maintenance run: the vault already runs the `weekly-maintenance` workflow
automatically every Sunday morning, so the agent just needs to attach to that
schedule and do its work after the maintenance pass finishes.

The agent reads across the whole vault, summarizes the week, writes
`40 Outputs/Weekly Digest <date>.md`, and then sends that file to my email address
so it reaches my phone.

## What it must never do

It is **read-only over my knowledge**. It never archives, edits, deletes, or
re-files anything — the digest only describes. The single file it writes is its own
output. If the summary is wrong I want to fix my notes, not discover the agent
already "helpfully" fixed them for me.

## Why an agent

A digest needs judgment — deciding what mattered this week is not something a
script can do. Agents are the component type for judgment work, so this is an
agent.

## Scope

- One page, five sections, no configuration in v1.
- Sunday only. No daily version, no on-demand version.
- Plain markdown. No HTML mail, no attachments, no images.

## Definition of done

- The digest arrives Sunday morning without me asking.
- It is accurate: every claim in it traces to something that actually changed.
- It never modifies knowledge.
